annotations.title: Findings about a node, with their evidence strength

description: Lists the curated study findings for one node by id, from search_nodes: for a compound, organism or material, what it has been shown to affect; for an outcome, which compounds have been studied against it. Use it to browse a node by id. For a question in words, such as "does X help Y", find_evidence answers in one call and needs no id. summary has one row per thing the node has findings about, counted over all its findings and not only the rows returned. The default number of findings, strongest first, is enough to answer. There is no offset: to see a different slice, pass about (an id from summary, or words such as "sleep") or evidence_strength. Each finding carries its evidence strength, one of five named levels from strong to insufficient (strong, moderate, limited, very_limited, insufficient), the verbatim sentence it was drawn from, the paper, the population and dose, and a permalink. An evidence strength says how well the evidence supports the finding and is not a recommendation; give it with the claim, and link the permalink. An empty list means no findings are recorded for that node, a complete answer that does not show the compound does nothing; empty_means says why.

about.description: Optional: only findings about this, as an id from summary (e.g. CAT:outcome/sleep-onset-latency) or words in its name (e.g. "sleep").

detail.description: brief (default) returns each finding with its claim, evidence strength, design, population, dose, quote, paper, permalink and a citation to quote as it stands. full adds every other recorded field and is longer; use it only when the person asks for all fields.

evidence_strength.description: Optional floor: only findings at this evidence strength or stronger, from strong down to insufficient.

limit.description: Findings to return, strongest evidence first (1 to 50). The default is enough to answer.

node_id.description: A node id in the form PREFIX:local, e.g. CHEBI:16919 (creatine). Get it from the id field of a search_nodes hit.
